tagline: The road the regulars marched out on, and ran back along.
intro: The byway starts in Arlington at the site of the Black Horse Tavern, where three committee members woke around three in the morning of April 19, 1775, to British troops marching past, and slipped out the back. Massachusetts Avenue carries on northwest through Lexington, and North Great Road runs through Lincoln to Concord, about fourteen miles on the approximate line of the regulars' march.

By afternoon the same road was the way back. Skirmishes dogged the column for the next eighteen miles, and in Lincoln two sharp bends, the first now called the Bloody Angle, cost the British thirty men killed or wounded.

moments.title: Lexington Battle Green
moments.text: Seventy-seven Lexington militiamen formed up on this triangle of grass, and to this day nobody is sure which side fired first.

moments.title: Paul Revere Capture Site
moments.text: The midnight ride ended here on Route 2A, where a British patrol took Paul Revere and Samuel Prescott jumped his horse over a wall and carried the word on to Concord.

moments.title: North Bridge and Muster Field
moments.text: From the Muster Field about 400 militiamen saw smoke over Concord and marched down to the bridge, where Major John Buttrick gave colonists their first order to fire on British troops.
